before it does. The section inventory and our compliance standard RE-FH-9 are both in

please — the print vendor's importer takes the two columns and chokes on anything more.

legal can sign off without re-reading RE-FH-9 themselves.

- `flagged_count` — sections whose `finding` is not `none`
- `personal_narrative_count`, `protected_lang_count`, `disclaimer_missing_count` — sections
  whose `finding` includes that label

---

Save all three into your current working directory, at exactly those filenames. Writing them
is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.

# Fair-housing audit — seller's book (RE-FH-9)

Audit of every section in `input/seller_book_sections.csv` against standard **RE-FH-9**,
including the **2026 amendments (§5)** that govern any book entering print from Q1 2026 and
that override the standing sections where they conflict. The book has not been re-templated
for the amendments, so several "official-looking" paragraphs now fail — see the abridged-notice
trap below.

Findings per section are in `fairhousing_audit.csv`; sign-off counts are in `results.json`.
This memo states the rules applied and the reason for each flag so sign-off does not require
re-reading RE-FH-9.

## Rules applied

**Required disclosure classes (11).** Per §2 the protected classes are race, colour, religion,
sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation and veteran status. Per
**§5a (2026)** the carried disclosure must **also name marital status and source of income**.
A notice naming anything fewer than all eleven is *abridged*. We audited against this amended
list, not against the paragraph the book happens to carry.

**§1 — Personal-narrative solicitation → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`.** Any section, in any
role, that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to
buyer identity. Phrases that triggered this: "write us a letter about what brought you here,"
"send a personal note about yourself," "include a short personal note about themselves and why
this home suits them," "covering letter introducing yourself," "tell us about yourselves."

**§2 — Protected-class language → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.** Names a protected class or a
proxy. Per §2 proxies count: houses of worship / churches, parish or faith schools (and parish
halls), and describing a street or block by the kind of household that lives on it reach
religion and familial status just as the bare terms do. In this book the tripping proxies are
"churches within walking distance," "parish school," "parish hall," "churchgoing households,"
"congregation-centred," "faith community," "family-oriented street," "young families,"
"long-established families," "toddler group."

**§3 — Mandated-disclosure exception (narrow).** A section is exempt from §2 *for the disclosure
text it carries* **only if** its notice names every one of the 11 required classes. An abridged
notice earns **no exemption at all** — so the protected-class words it does list count as
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, however official the section looks and whatever its role. The
exemption covers §2 only; §1 and §4 still apply. Protected-class terms used in a section's own
prose, outside the notice, are **never** covered.

**§4 — Required disclaimer → `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.** A section in a responsible role must carry a
compliant (all-11-class) notice; no notice, or an abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Per §4
the responsible role is `closing_page`; per **§5b (2026)** `agent_bio` now carries the same
responsibility. `listing_copy`, `seller_letter` and `disclosure_block` are **not** assessed
under §4 (so a `disclosure_block` with an abridged notice is not `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` — but see
§3 for its §2 exposure).

### The abridged-notice trap (the main thing legal needs to understand)

The standing disclosure paragraph in circulation names ten classes — race, colour, religion,
sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, **veteran status** — and
stops there. Because §5a added **marital status** and **source of income**, that ten-class
paragraph is now **abridged**. It has two independent consequences, both intended by the standard:

1. **§4:** any responsible section (`closing_page` or `agent_bio`) carrying it — or a shorter
   cut-down — is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` until the template is reissued.
2. **§3:** because the notice is abridged it loses its §2 exemption, so the protected-class
   words it *does* list (race, religion, sex, etc.) now read as `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. This
   bites even a `disclosure_block` that is not §4-responsible — "however official it looks."

The fix in every case is the same: replace the carried notice with one that names all eleven
classes. Once a notice is complete, the §2 exemption is restored for the disclosure text and §4
is satisfied; only a section's *own* prose outside the notice can then still trip §2.

## Per-section findings

Only flagged sections are listed; everything else is `none`. Labels are joined in the order
`PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE | PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING`, matching the
audit CSV.

| Section | Role | Finding | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-02 | seller_letter | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | "write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you." |
| SEC-03 | listing_copy | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | "family-oriented street" (familial-status proxy, street described by household kind); "two churches within walking distance" and "parish school" (religion proxies). |
| SEC-04 | disclosure_block | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | Carries a ten-class notice (no marital status / source of income) → abridged → no §3 exemption, so the classes it lists trip §2. Not §4-responsible, so no `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. |
| SEC-05 | closing_page | `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | Responsible role, no notice at all. Clean prose otherwise. |
| SEC-07 | closing_page | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE\|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE\|DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | "Send a personal note about yourself…" (§1); "churchgoing households" + "long-established families" (§2, religion + familial-status proxies); responsible role with no notice (§4). |
| SEC-08 | disclosure_block | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | "include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits them" (§1). Notice is complete (all 11) so §3 exempts its class terms; §1 is unaffected by the exemption. Not §4-responsible. |

| SEC-14 | agent_bio | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE\|DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | Same abridged-notice trap as SEC-11, in an `agent_bio` (§4-responsible via §5b). Clean own prose. |
| SEC-15 | closing_page | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE\|DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | Notice cut to four classes (race, colour, religion, sex) → abridged → §2 on the listed classes; responsible role → §4. |
| SEC-17 | seller_letter | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE\|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | "covering letter introducing yourself" (§1); "congregation-centred" + "faith community" (§2, religion). Not §4-responsible. |
| SEC-19 | closing_page | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | Complete 11-class notice (so §4 satisfied and notice terms exempt), but the section's **own prose** repeats "family-oriented street," "two churches within walking distance," "parish school" — never covered by the exemption. |
| SEC-21 | agent_bio | `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | `agent_bio` is §4-responsible (§5b) and carries no notice. Clean prose otherwise. |
| SEC-22 | disclosure_block | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | Six-class notice (stops at "national origin") → abridged → no §3 exemption → listed classes trip §2. Not §4-responsible. |
| SEC-24 | closing_page | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | "Tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what brought you here…" (§1). Notice is complete, so no §2/§4 finding. |
| SEC-25 | listing_copy | `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | "churchgoing households" + "long-established families" (§2, religion + familial status). |
| SEC-27 | seller_letter | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | "Send a personal note about yourself along with the offer…" (§1). Not §4-responsible. |
| SEC-29 | agent_bio | `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | "include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits them" (§1). Notice is complete, so §4 satisfied and notice terms exempt. |
| SEC-30 | closing_page | `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | Responsible role, no notice. Clean prose otherwise. |

Clean sections (finding `none`): SEC-01, SEC-06, SEC-10, SEC-12, SEC-13, SEC-16, SEC-18, SEC-20,
SEC-23, SEC-26, SEC-28.

## Sign-off counts

Counts are of **sections**, not labels (a section with several labels is counted once per
label it carries, and once in `flagged_count`):

- `section_count` — **30** (sections in the inventory)
- `flagged_count` — **19** (sections whose finding is not `none`)
- `personal_narrative_count` — **7** (SEC-02, SEC-07, SEC-08, SEC-17, SEC-24, SEC-27, SEC-29)
- `protected_lang_count` — **11** (SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-22, SEC-25)
- `disclaimer_missing_count` — **8** (SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-21, SEC-30)

## Recommended remediation before print

1. **Reissue the disclosure template** to name all eleven classes (add **marital status** and
   **source of income**). Drop the replacement into every `closing_page` and `agent_bio`. This
   alone clears every `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` and restores the §3 exemption (clearing §2 for
   SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-22).
2. **Strip the buyer-letter solicitations** from SEC-02, SEC-07, SEC-08, SEC-17, SEC-24,
   SEC-27, SEC-29 (§1 is not cured by any disclosure).
3. **Rewrite the neighbourhood/street prose** in SEC-03, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-25
   to remove the church/parish/congregation and family-household proxies. A complete notice
   does not cover these — they sit outside the notice.

Once 1–3 are done, re-run this audit; expected outcome is all `none`.
